text:
Last season Josh Doan quietly became one of Buffalo's most useful forwards: Evolving-Hockey had him at 2.2 wins above replacement, 42nd among 401 forwards, and his play-driving impact in the 97th percentile. This season has gone the other way, along with the Sabres; Sabre Noise ran "Josh Doan spotlighted as Buffalo Sabres slide in NHL Power Rankings."

He has 4 goals and 7 points in 22 games, and his ice time is down to about 14:15 over his last ten. The deeper concern is at five on five, where Buffalo gets only 44.8% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, 6 points worse than without him. Last season's numbers said the opposite.

There's some bad luck in the shooting. He's at 10.5% against a league norm of 13.4%, and our talent range puts his true scoring rate around 2.1 points per 60, well above his current 1.27. His net-front power-play tip against Tampa is the role to watch, and so is his five-on-five share: that's where last season's value lived.
